text:
maya.chen: Heads up — seeing ~7% capacity drop in us-west1 GPU pool (rack-12 cohort). PCIe reset counter spike + thermal variance on 4 cards. Dash: https://grafana.redwood/shot/us-west1/gpu-pci-resets
jordan: ack — looking. Do we have a correlated deployment or rolling maintenance?
infra-bot: alert: gpu.pcie.reset_rate high (us-west1-rack-12), threshold breached at 2026-06-12T15:12:05Z
priya.k: no planned maintenance. logs show repeated `PCIe link reset` and `nvlink timeout` on host gnode-12-3.
samuel: can you paste `dmesg` snippets? wondering if it's firmware vs hw.
maya.chen: pasted minimal `dmesg` sample:
```
[Jun12 15:10:12] pcieport 0000:3e:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: ID 0x0001
[Jun12 15:10:12] NVRM: Xid(13): GPU has fallen off the bus
[Jun12 15:11:34] nvidia 0000:3f:00.0: Nvlink: peer timeout, resetting link
```
tasha: thermal sensors also show short spikes to 90C on one card then back to 64C within 30s — looks like intermittent sensor flapping rather than sustained overtemp.
jordan: interesting — could be transient power rail glitch or cabling on that PCI riser. Are these hosts all on the same PDUs?
priya.k: yes, gnode-12-* are on pdu-c-2 (PDUID: PDU-12C). Power logs show no bulk outages, but PDU outlet current has tiny blips.
samuel: quick triage plan — isolate 3 affected nodes, drain them from serving pool, repro on spare host with same riser/pdu, swap riser/cable if reproducible. Can infra do a coord drain?
maya.chen: initiating partial drain for rack-12 (impact-target <=10% traffic). Will post drain IDs.
infra-bot: drain initiated: drain-id=drain-20260612-15-22, nodes: gnode-12-1,gnode-12-2,gnode-12-3. ETA 3m.
sre-oncall: pinging hardware-ops for on-site PDU check @hardware-ops. Can someone start a replacement-swap window for gnode-12-3?
jordan: I'll queue a swap. Also increasing telemetry sampling to 1s for PCIe and thermal on those nodes (config: `telemetry.sample_rate=1s`).
priya.k: after drain, error rate dropped to baseline but one replacement test still produced `Xid(13)`. We swapped PCIe riser on gnode-12-3 in the lab and re-ran stress, no issues so far.
samuel: that points to intermittent cabling/connector issue in rack. Recommend rolling physical inspection and reseat on remaining eight nodes in that PDU group.
maya.chen: agree. Cost note: reseat ops ~2hr tech time, lost capacity ~5% during ops window. Heads-up to product: may see slight throughput dip.
tasha: I'll file a short post-op note to infra-runbook and add a runbook step to bump telemetry windows when PCIe resets spike.
priya.k: also adding automatic fallback policy to route latency-sensitive requests off the affected pool when PCIe.reset_count > 5/min (policy draft: `route.policy.pcie_surge_threshold`).
jordan: nice — reminder to include model-specific lower-priority routing for big embeddings jobs so they don't hit the degraded pool.
infra-bot: alert resolved: gpu.pcie.reset_rate reduced below threshold at 2026-06-12T15:48:11Z (cause: local reseat + cable swap).
maya.chen: marking thread for follow-up doc with checklist + PDU inspection notes. Thanks all :thumbsup:
priya.k: follow-up task created: #TASK-4893 "rack-12 PDU cable reseat + telemetry tweak" assigned to hardware-ops. ETA EOD tomorrow.
sre-oncall: closing oncall loop; re-open if we see recurrence.
